# Indriya Saṁyutta (SN 48)

**ID:** SN 48
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Indriya Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The five faculties are frequently analyzed in complementary pairings—faith with wisdom, and energy with concentration, overseen and balanced by mindfulness [Bodhi 2003]. The collection concludes with repetition series framed according to seclusion and the removal of lust [Bodhi 2003].

Key discourses define the individual faculties and their soteriological functions. In the *Daṭṭhabbasutta* (SN 48.8), the faculties are mapped to their respective spheres, such as faith being understood through the four factors of stream-attainment [Gethin 2001; Ledi Sayadaw 1971]. In the *Vibhaṅgasuttas* (SN 48.9–10), mindfulness is defined by recollection of long-past deeds and words, concentration by unification of mind attained through letting go (*vossaggārammaṇaṁ karitvā*), and wisdom by insight into arising and vanishing leading to the destruction of suffering [Gyatso 1992; Anālayo 2019; Bodhi 2012; Wen; Gaffney 2003]. In SN 48.24, the strengths of these faculties differentiate three classes of stream-enterers (*ekabījin*, *kolamkola*, and *sattakkhattuparama*) [Wen].

Parallels to suttas in the *Indriyasaṁyutta* are preserved extensively in Chinese translation, notably across fifteen discourses in the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99 / SĀ), including SĀ 643 (to SN 48.1), SĀ 646 (to SN 48.8), SĀ 647 (to SN 48.9–10), and SĀ 652–654 [Wen]. DharmaNexus records substantial Pali-internal text reuse with the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), *Aṅguttaranikāya* collections, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (*Indriyakathā*), and Abhidhamma texts like the *Yamaka* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus reflect shared doctrinal formulas with the Sanskrit *Śrāvakabhūmi*, Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya*, the *Daśottarasūtra*, and Tibetan translations of canonical works and commentarial treatises such as the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣyaṭīkā Upāyikā* and *Arthaviniścayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
